name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+15 partisan lean
Incumbent Troy Balderson running with $2.0M cash on hand
Democrat Jerrad Christian raised only $84K with no outside spending
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Balderson: a heavily Republican district, incumbency, and a dominant financial edge over a challenger who has raised little. Markets and the lack of any competitive signals confirm a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: A surge of Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a polling surprise, would be the first sign this race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Balderson seeks another term in a central Ohio district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. He enters the general election with roughly two million dollars on hand after raising over $1.7 million, while Democrat Jerrad Christian has raised under $85,000 and reports no outside support. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Balderson about a 95 percent chance of winning.

The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage leaves little evidence of a competitive race. The forecast expects Balderson to win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
